text:
For many years I have sought the wilderness,

for many years I have lived sadly,

for many years I have been ill,

and it is because of the book you wrote!


O Kempis, before reading you I loved

the light, the meadows, the Ocean Sea;

but you said that everything ends,

that everything dies, that everything is vain!


Before, carried by my desires,

I kissed lips that invite a kiss,

the blond braids, the large eyes,

without remembering that they wither!


But since grave doctors affirm,

whom you, master, cite and name,

that man passes like ships,

like clouds, like shadows…


I flee every earthly bond,

no affection gladdens my mind,

and with your book under my arm

I go traversing the black night…


O Kempis, Kempis, barren ascetic,

pale ascetic, how you harmed me!

For many years I have been ill,

and it is because of the book you wrote!

translation.title: For Many Years I Have Sought the Wilderness...
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the playful accusation against Kempis and the repeated refrain about the book that made the speaker ill.
